description: Experience the joy of a true Italian breakfast with our authentic Cornetto recipe. These buttery, flaky croissants are a staple in Italy, perfect for dipping in your morning cappuccino or enjoying with jam. Master the art of laminating dough to create these delightful pastries right in your own kitchen.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm milk, sugar, and active dry yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. Add the flour, salt, egg, and vanilla extract (if using) to the yeast mixture. Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then knead on a lightly floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Chill and Prepare Butter Block
instructions.text: Once the dough has risen, gently deflate it and shape it into a rectangle. Wrap it tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight. While the dough chills, prepare your butter block. Place the cold butter between two sheets of parchment paper and pound it with a rolling pin to flatten it into a 15x15 cm (6x6 inch) square. Keep it chilled until ready to use.

instructions.title: First Fold (Single Turn)
instructions.text: On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled dough into a rectangle about 40x20 cm (16x8 inches). Place the butter block in the center of the dough. Fold one side of the dough over the butter, then fold the other side over, completely enclosing the butter. Pinch the edges to seal. Rotate the dough 90 degrees, so the seam is on your left. Roll it out again to a 40x20 cm rectangle. Fold it into thirds, like a business letter. This is your first 'single turn'. Wrap the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Second and Third Folds
instructions.text: Repeat the rolling and folding process (single turn) two more times. Each time, ensure the dough is rotated 90 degrees before rolling and folding. After each fold, wrap the dough tightly and refrigerate for 30 minutes. This creates the flaky layers characteristic of a Cornetto. After the third fold, refrigerate the dough for at least 1 hour, or up to overnight.

instructions.title: Shape the Cornetti
instructions.text: On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled dough into a large rectangle, about 3-4 mm thick. Trim the edges to create a perfect rectangle. Cut the rectangle into long triangles with a base of about 8-10 cm (3-4 inches). Starting from the base of each triangle, gently roll it up towards the tip, creating the classic Cornetto shape. Slightly curve the ends to form a crescent. Place the shaped Cornetti on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.

instructions.title: Final Proof and Bake
instructions.text: Cover the shaped Cornetti loosely with plastic wrap and let them proof in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until visibly puffy. They should almost double in size. Preheat your oven to 190C (375F). Lightly beat an egg with a tablespoon of water for an egg wash. Gently brush the tops of the Cornetti with the egg wash. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and flaky. Let them cool slightly on a wire rack before serving.

tips: Use high-quality, cold butter for lamination; it makes a significant difference in flakiness and flavor. European-style butter with higher fat content is ideal.
Do not rush the chilling steps between folds. Proper chilling ensures the butter stays cold and distinct from the dough, creating crisp layers.
Serve Cornetti warm, perhaps with a dusting of powdered sugar, or filled with jam, Nutella, or pastry cream for a true Italian experience.
